stage: 6c. Run day to day: change, support and incidents

summary.text: Every network pushes change through gated bulletins on a fixed calendar. Visa emails weekly Visa Business News to two named roles, Mastercard posts numbered announcements on its login-only Technical Resource Center.

American Express publishes a monthly Network Participant Updates bulletin and April and October manuals. Discover updates its programme documents twice a year, and processors report dated April Discover and PULSE releases.

The primary bulletins are private. Visa says its Business News articles are not public, Mastercard bulletins reach only members through Mastercard Connect, and PULSE publishes no rules or bulletins on its public site.

Most partners meet change second hand. Issuer processors republish each mandate with an impact note, and merchant processors count continued use as acceptance. One credit union CUSO asks clients to forward network mail.

American Express types each change as policy, legal or information only and publishes a route to a three-month extension. Visa waivers go through a representative and Mastercard variances through Variance Manager.

Support runs through phone desks, mailboxes and named account executives. Mastercard and Visa describe 24x7 client support teams, Discover splits a 24x7 command centre from a business-hours operations centre, and PULSE publishes Central-time business hours only.

No public status page for core authorisation and settlement was found for any of the four networks. Public status pages cover developer APIs and gateway products, and Amex posts urgent bulletins inside its Knowledge Base.

The clearest public account of incident communication failure is Visa's June 2018 outage. An independent review found its communications were not timely, regular or actionable, and the UK regulator now requires annual testing with participants.

Acquirers feel the strain most. The UK regulator found acquirers holding over 65 percent of the market struggle to get timely answers, and a US payfac filing calls network compliance timelines highly compressed.
Discover and PULSE change lightly. Two issuer processors say recent Discover and PULSE mandates did not affect them or their clients, which is an asset the network does not yet present.

how_it_works.text: Visa sends weekly Visa Business News by email to each member's Primary Center Manager and Senior Officer. The Primary Center Manager must distribute it inside the bank.
Members register these roles in the My Organization's Contacts module of the Client Directory in Visa Access. Updates are due within 10 business days of a change.
A Business News article carries an article ID, a region and audience line, a brand line and an overview with the effective date.
Visa corrects an article by republishing it with a note on what changed.
A Visa Notification takes effect when Visa sends it, so a missed email is still a received notice.
Regional implementation analysts project-manage the twice-yearly business enhancement releases and Visa mandates for clients and processors.
A bank that cannot comply asks for a waiver through its Visa representative. Visa answers in writing, each waiver is unique, and an extension carries an assessment.
For log-in and technical issues users go to their own delegated administrators first, then a regional Visa Access Support team by email or phone.
Issuers and acquirers without Visa Access are told to contact their Visa account executive or manager.
A Client Success manager owns post-sale service and a Client Success Plan, separate from the account team.
During issuer outages Visa's Smarter Stand-In Processing authorises on the issuer's behalf.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Access (formerly Visa Online)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Password-protected client site for members and processors, claiming 150+ services, with a built-in help centre and AI search.

tools_and_screens.name: Client Directory: My Organization's Contacts
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Where a member names its Primary Center Manager and Senior Officer, who then receive Visa Business News.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Business News
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Weekly email bulletin with article ID, region, audience, brand and effective-dated overview.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Resolve Online
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Mandated web application for dispute life-cycle work by issuer and acquirer staff.

friction.text: There is no public archive of Visa Business News, so anyone outside the two named roles depends on internal forwarding.
During the June 2018 outage Visa's methods for reaching clients were found not effective or efficient.
Waiver extensions cost money and set no precedent, so each bank relitigates similar requests.

how_it_works.text: Mastercard defines its Standards to include announcements and bulletins, which is how rule changes take effect.
Announcements are posted in the Technical Resource Center on Mastercard Connect. Each has a structured header with type, audience, region, action indicator, published and effective dates.
Each rulebook edition opens with a summary of changes mapped to numbered announcements with regional prefixes.
Network releases are named by year and quarter, with major releases in April and October.
Urgent issues go by phone to Customer Technical Services. Non-urgent ones go to a Support Case Management tool.
Customer Technical Services is described as a single point of contact giving first and second level support around the clock.
Technology account managers run Quarterly Operational Reviews for key accounts and train customers on releases.
In an incident the account manager joins the response team, relays updates, and later shares Mastercard's Post Incident Report.
A bank that cannot meet a Standard requests a variance through Variance Manager on Mastercard Connect.
Noncompliance assessments can be appealed to the Chief Franchise Officer within 30 days, for a fee of up to USD 500.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercard Connect
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Sign-in wall with RSA SecurID for Mastercom, Technical Resource Center, My Company Manager and Variance Manager.

tools_and_screens.name: Technical Resource Center
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Announcements and bulletins, plus guides such as the Chargeback Guide and Mastercom User Guide.

tools_and_screens.name: Support Case Management
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Case application on Mastercard Connect for non-urgent support.

tools_and_screens.name: Variance Manager
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Tool for requesting a variance from a Standard.

friction.text: The Technical Resource Center returns a 404 to unauthenticated visitors, so change news reaches the public only through practitioners.
Mastercard's Atlassian status page appears to be an unpopulated template.
Quarterly reviews appear in postings for key accounts only, so smaller issuers may never see one. That is inference.

how_it_works.text: Network Participant Updates publish monthly on the second Friday, and Special Bulletins cover urgent issues.
The Business and Operational Policies manual is republished every April and October and posted to Knowledge Base.
Each change is typed Policy, Legally required or Information only.
Policy changes take effect on publication. A participant that cannot comply documents the impact and requests up to three months' extension, which Amex says it will not unreasonably withhold.
Technical specification changes are announced six months ahead in a twice-yearly Notification of Specification Changes.
Participants sign an annual attestation of accuracy for Program Progress Reports.
An issuer schedules its own outages by phoning the AEGNS Help Desk, ideally 30 days ahead, and must report unscheduled outages at once.
Violations follow a determination, notification and Action Plan process with escalating fees.
Training is requested through the Amex representative or a named mailbox and assigned by Knowledge Base profile.
Amex commits to process Knowledge Base access requests within three business days.

tools_and_screens.name: Knowledge Base
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Login-gated portal with search, bookmarks, Participant Directory and a 'Request Additional Services' route to OpsNet, File Tracker and FraudNet.

tools_and_screens.name: Urgent Bulletins page
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Inside Knowledge Base, where urgent operational communications are posted.

tools_and_screens.name: Participant Directory
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Shared directory of participants' key contacts, which participants must keep current.

friction.text: The public GNS contact route is a web form that issues a case number, with no phone or hours.
The public webinar list has not been updated since 2022.
The manual describes how participants must report their outages to Amex, and says little about how Amex reports its own.

how_it_works.text: Discover publishes updates to its programme documents twice a year, or more often when needed.
Processors report a dated April 2026 Discover Release with numbered sections.
Issuer client support is split by product line, with separate toll-free numbers for credit, debit and prepaid issuers.
Unresolved fraud questions go through a named Discover Network Relationship Manager.
Partners must phone Discover Global Network Security within 48 hours of a data compromise.
Diners Club issuers use a ServiceNow-hosted portal limited to existing issuers.

tools_and_screens.name: Service Center login
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Single MFA login for fraud tooling and client portals, with a fraud-specialist hotline.

tools_and_screens.name: Fraud and Risk Center enrolments
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Application PDFs and web forms for Account Incident Manager, Confirmed Fraud Portal, Fraud Alerts and High Brand Risk.

tools_and_screens.name: Diners Club issuer portal
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: ServiceNow site for current Diners Club issuers.

friction.text: Client services are spread across function-specific mailboxes.
Non-US partners get a single contact mailbox.
No public source shows a Discover issuer bulletin, so its format and lead times cannot be judged.

best_pattern.text: American Express types every change and states a documented extension route with a three-month ceiling. It is the clearest published model of what a change asks and what to do when a partner cannot comply.

discover_today.text: Discover offers segmented phone lines and a relationship manager, but its issuer change channel is not public and its contact model leans on many mailboxes.

by_partner.partner_type: Community banks and credit unions (small issuers, through processors and CUSOs)

how_it_works.text: Visa still routes community banks and credit unions to Visa Online for enrolment in products and the Merchant Offers Program.
An Associate member operates under a Principal for settlement, reporting and fees.
Visa Business News goes to each member's Primary Center Manager, a role a small card team may share with other duties. That is inference.
Processors read the bulletins on their behalf. A Velera dispute supervisor reviews Visa, Mastercard and other network mandates for its credit union clients.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Online community issuer enrolment
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Product enrolment portal at secure.visaonline.com, still called Visa Online on the community issuer page.

friction.text: New network features wait on the core provider. One community bank said debit tokenisation was stalled while it waited.
Smaller institutions struggle to absorb core provider charges for updates.

how_it_works.text: Issuer processors certify against each Mastercard release and republish the bulletins they support by GLB number and effective date.

tools_and_screens.name: Processor mandate pages
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public processor pages listing each Mastercard bulletin with its effective date and an impact note.

friction.text: A small issuer sees Mastercard change only as its processor frames it. That is inference.

how_it_works.text: PULSE runs persona support desks, including a PULSE Issuer Support line, a separate Discover Debit issuer line and an account-management mailbox.
Published PULSE hours are business hours in Central time. The only response commitment is a two-business-day callback on web requests.
Portal credentials are issued within five business days through a manual three-step process.
PULSE releases are dated. Processors report an April 2026 PULSE Release effective 12 April.
PULSE runs an annual Voice of the Client survey and a client newsletter.

tools_and_screens.name: PULSE client tools
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Debit Dashboard, ATM List Manager, Marketing Hub and PULSE Exchange behind one Log In / Register.

tools_and_screens.name: PULSE Client Support page
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public page naming desks, phone numbers and mailboxes by partner type.

friction.text: PULSE operating rules and bulletins are not public, and its news page has not been updated since August 2024.
There is no published 24x7 line or formal service level.

how_it_works.text: SHAZAM, a member-owned network and processor, staffs client service 24/7/365 and takes Service Expert requests in its SHAZAM Access portal.
Its login menu includes a status tool, SHAZAM SystemChek, beside file and ATM monitoring tools.
A client learning team runs live webinars and on-demand courses inside SHAZAM Access.

tools_and_screens.name: SHAZAM Access and SystemChek
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Client portal with service requests, and a gated system status tool.

friction.text: SystemChek is gated, so its content could not be inspected.

how_it_works.text: CU*Answers, a core CUSO, says network vendors send mandates with required programming changes and short deadlines.
It asks credit unions to forward network communications to its Cards and Payments team so it can keep everyone informed.
A credit union card services manager is the primary liaison with processors, networks and rewards providers.

tools_and_screens.name: CUSO mandate review page
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public page explaining mandates, with a forwarding mailbox and client news.

friction.text: A mandate can reach a credit union through its EFT processor, its core CUSO and its own inbox, and the CUSO relies on forwarded copies.

best_pattern.text: SHAZAM pairs round-the-clock client service with an in-portal status tool. Issuer processors that state per release what changed and that no action is needed give small teams the clearest signal.

discover_today.text: PULSE offers named issuer desks and dated releases, but business-hours support, stale public news and no public bulletins leave small issuers reliant on their processor.

how_it_works.text: Acquirers must retrieve the Visa Acceptance Risk Standards and risk communications from Visa Online themselves.
Visa's own processing arm, Visa Acceptance Solutions, supports clients by chat, case or phone depending on agreement.
It runs a public Atlassian status page with email and SMS subscriptions and a monthly incident history.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Acceptance status page
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Production and sandbox components with subscriptions and incident history.

tools_and_screens.name: Business Center support cases
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Case types General Support Request and MID Configuration Request.

friction.text: The retrieval duty sits with the acquirer, with no public signal when a standard changes.
Visa Acceptance asks clients to open a sandbox case only after two hours of instability with no incident posted.

how_it_works.text: Product change notices on the developer portal give separate test and production effective dates and point to the gated announcement.
Mastercard Send publishes a quarterly release calendar with notes three months ahead and a peak-season change freeze.
At implementation a named Delivery Manager is assigned.
Ethoca support splits response by severity, two to four hours for a production outage.

tools_and_screens.name: API Status page
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Per-service Sandbox and Production health for about 100 services, polled about once a minute.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercom announcements
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Dated API change notices with test and production dates.

friction.text: Rule bulletins stay behind Mastercard Connect, so large acquirers staff teams to translate them into system requirements.
UK acquirers said pricing bulletin codes in the scheme portals do not match the codes on invoices.

how_it_works.text: Specification changes are pre-announced six months ahead in the twice-yearly NOSC, with Technical Bulletins for off-cycle items.
If the network stops responding, the acquirer is told to phone the AEGNS technical Help Desk.
OptBlue programme changes reach acquirers' sales agents through a public site with update PDFs and an email list.

tools_and_screens.name: OptBlue Sales Agent site
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public training resources, programme-update PDFs and opt-in email list.

friction.text: Detection of a network outage is left to the acquirer.

how_it_works.text: Acquirers and processors use the EASI Portal for specifications, test card kits, announcements and a Message Center to operations.
The Operations Center keeps US business hours, while connectivity incidents go to a 24x7 Network Command Center with a second-escalation manager.
A named Account Executive is the escalation point for daily operations and owns contracts, upgrades and configuration changes.
The detailed IIN range table sits in the EASI Document Library for companies with an NDA.
Discover periodically sends acquirers a short compliance questionnaire.
PULSE processors and acquirers share one support number with separate mailboxes.

tools_and_screens.name: EASI Portal
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Specifications, test card kits, product announcements, Document Library and Message Center, behind registration.

tools_and_screens.name: Release Compliance Tool
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Gated Discover test and certification tool listed on Partner Resources.

friction.text: The operations desk closes on twelve US holidays and keeps Eastern business hours.

best_pattern.text: Regulated notice periods set the bar: six months for UK fee changes and 120 days in Canada. Braintree's table of type, network, region and date shows the format acquirers relay.

discover_today.text: Discover gives acquirers a portal message centre, a 24x7 command centre and a named account executive. Public evidence of its change notices is limited to processor reports.

how_it_works.text: Most agents are registered by a sponsoring issuer or acquirer, which acts as liaison with Visa.
Merchants and agents are told to contact their acquirer about Business News items.

tools_and_screens.name: Program Request Management
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Acquirer application in Visa Access used to register each payment facilitator.

friction.text: Payfacs learn of Visa changes through their sponsor, and filings describe compressed timelines.
A payfac filing says networks can change rules with or without advance notice.

how_it_works.text: Mandates that change payfac monitoring, such as sub-merchant level chargeback monitoring from April 2027, are known publicly only through practitioner reports.

friction.text: Large payment firms staff a card network office to read releases and run waiver requests.

how_it_works.text: Amex's international merchant regulations give at least 30 days' notice of rule changes and treat continued acceptance as agreement.
The October 2025 rules added portfolio accountability and escalating fees for intermediaries.

tools_and_screens.name: OptBlue Sales Agent site
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public programme-update PDFs and email list for agents.

friction.text: Intermediaries face fees of up to USD 20,000 for repeat violations.

how_it_works.text: Payment enablers that handle Discover card data must submit a PCI attestation every year, by email to the DISC team.

friction.text: Compliance filing runs through a shared mailbox with no status view. That is inference.

best_pattern.text: Amex's public OptBlue agent site with update PDFs and an email list reaches sales agents who have no network login.

discover_today.text: Discover's payfac relationship shows publicly only as PCI filing by email. No public payfac change channel was found.

how_it_works.text: Processor CDS relayed Visa's 18 October 2025 operator rules and warned of suspension and network fines.
No public PLUS rulebook or ATM-operator surface was found.

tools_and_screens.name: Processor news notices
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: CDS news posts that restate network rules for independent operators.

friction.text: Operators receive rules and fines second hand, and CDS passes network fines through to the ISO.

how_it_works.text: PULSE offers an ATM List Manager among its client tools.

tools_and_screens.name: ATM List Manager
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Gated PULSE tool named on the Client Support page.

friction.text: PULSE publishes no operating rules, so operators cannot see the obligations directly.

how_it_works.text: The National ATM Council's jackpotting guidance lists police and federal agencies as contacts and names no card network.

friction.text: No network incident contact appears in the operators' own security guidance.

best_pattern.text: No strong public pattern was found. The processor notice that names rules, dates and consequences is the closest usable format.

discover_today.text: PULSE reaches operators through gated tools and processors, with no public rules.

how_it_works.text: Visa Partner support is a single email alias for website and account questions.
Issuer processors certify each VisaNet Business Enhancements release and tell programme managers what they changed.

tools_and_screens.name: Processor certification pages
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Per-release list of mandates, what the processor did and whether client action is needed.

friction.text: Visa's peer developer community no longer resolves.

how_it_works.text: SoFi Tech Solutions lists each Mastercard bulletin by number with an impact paragraph naming the API field affected.

friction.text: Networks send processors technical documents four times a year, and the programme manager relies on the processor's reading.

how_it_works.text: Marqeta certifies Discover and PULSE releases and labels them changes with no impact on the card programme.
For October 2026 Marqeta records no applicable Discover or PULSE changes.

friction.text: Developer Center access and collaborator invites depend on a Discover representative.

best_pattern.text: A per-release impact note that names the field, states whether the client must act and says when nothing is needed.

discover_today.text: Discover's light mandate load reaches fintechs as a line saying nothing applies, which processors write and Discover does not.

how_it_works.text: Visa Developer publishes monthly release notes back to 2017, and the newest entry was May 2026 when checked.
The home page carried a mandatory certificate renewal notice with dated cutovers, and Visa emails owners of production projects before certificates expire.
The only published support channel is developer@visa.com, with no hours or response commitment.

tools_and_screens.name: Release notes
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Monthly entries tagged Public or Restricted.

Direct tickets require sign-in, while the forum is readable logged out.
Mastercom keys expire every 13 months and customers must track expiry and subscribe several users to notices.

tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Healthy, Partially Degraded, Unreachable and Not available states with a last 24 hours column.

friction.text: Change cadence differs by product.

how_it_works.text: Developer support is a ServiceNow ticket system with published hours and certificate turnaround commitments.

tools_and_screens.name: Create Support Ticket
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Form with seven categories and two attachments, usable without login.

friction.text: Nothing in the portal references a status page.

how_it_works.text: Partner Product Portal specs are public and include a healthcheck operation.

tools_and_screens.name: Partner Product Portal API Specs tab
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public OpenAPI documents per product.

friction.text: There is no published developer support service level.

discover_today.text: Discover exposes public specs but gates access and support on a representative.

by_partner.partner_type: Merchants dealing with the network directly

how_it_works.text: Visa publishes a merchant digest of Business News with month and region tags and a subscription form.
Readers are told to contact a Visa representative or their acquirer.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Merchant Business News Digest
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public list of summaries by month and region, newest May 2026 when checked.

friction.text: The public merchant support page is a document library with no contact channel.

how_it_works.text: Directly signed merchants get a phone line on weekday hours, a 24/7 authorisation line and chat after login.
Rule changes come in a Notification of Changes document each April and October, with overview, effective date and implications.
Data incidents go to the Enterprise Incident Response Program within 72 hours.

tools_and_screens.name: Online Merchant Account
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Settlements, disputes, statements and chat for direct merchants.

friction.text: Full merchant regulations sit behind the merchant login.

how_it_works.text: Discover runs a 24/7 voice line for authorisations and address checks.
Chip-enabled merchants with a tested incident plan can apply for relief from PCI paperwork through SCIP.

friction.text: Merchants acquired elsewhere must go to their acquirer for compliance questions.

how_it_works.text: Fiserv's merchant notice lists network fee changes and says continued use after 30 days means acceptance.
Braintree says most updates need no merchant action but some force integration work or fees.

tools_and_screens.name: Processor card brand update pages
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public notices restating network fee and rule changes for merchants.

friction.text: The Fiserv notice opens with a general warning and does not state which merchants are affected.

best_pattern.text: Amex's Notification of Changes gives each change an overview, effective date, merchant implications and the new text in one document.

discover_today.text: Discover offers merchants a 24/7 voice line and PCI relief, with no public merchant change digest found.

design_moves.title: Change ledger with a verdict per partner
design_moves.move: Publish every rule, fee and specification change as one ledger item typed action, legal or information, with audience, region and effective date. Show each partner a verdict: acts, processor has handled it, or nothing needed.
design_moves.why_advantage: Amex types changes and Mastercard headers carry action indicators, but no network tells a partner whether its processor has already absorbed the work. Processors write that sentence today.

design_moves.title: Notices built to be forwarded
design_moves.move: Render each change as a shareable page with a public summary and role-specific views for processor, institution and merchant. Let a processor or CUSO subscribe clients and see who opened it.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa and Mastercard bulletins are private, and a CUSO relies on clients forwarding network mail. A forwardable notice makes the relay chain part of the network's own product.

design_moves.title: Stated lead times on every change
design_moves.move: Commit to a minimum notice period for fee and mandate changes worldwide, show it on each item, and flag any item that falls short with the reason.
design_moves.why_advantage: Acquirers and payfacs describe compressed timelines. The UK now requires six months and Canada 120 days, so a global commitment turns regulation into a promise.

design_moves.title: Extension request inside the change
design_moves.move: Attach a request-more-time action to each change, with the decision rule stated up front and a tracked status.
design_moves.why_advantage: Amex publishes a three-month extension route that will not be unreasonably withheld. Visa routes waivers through a representative with a fee, and large PSPs staff people to chase waivers.

design_moves.title: Partner status for the core network
design_moves.move: Run a partner status view for authorisation, settlement, portals and APIs, with subscriptions, a declared update rhythm during incidents and a post-incident report every partner can read.
design_moves.why_advantage: Networks publish status only for APIs and gateway products. Visa's 2018 communications failed, while Mastercard shares post-incident reports only through account managers.

design_moves.title: One support map with hours and clocks
design_moves.move: Publish one support map by partner type and problem, each route with hours and a response commitment, and a round-the-clock path for small institutions.
design_moves.why_advantage: Discover and PULSE spread support across many mailboxes and business-hours desks. Acquirers struggle to get timely answers, and SHAZAM shows small institutions value 24/7 service.

design_moves.title: Contacts that stay current
design_moves.move: Let partners assign roles for change, incident and compliance notices, send each notice to several people, and prompt a review when a contact bounces or goes quiet.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa's rules treat a notice as received when sent and rely on two named roles. Mastercard leaves credential expiry tracking to customers.

design_moves.title: A quiet cycle, said plainly
design_moves.move: When a release asks nothing of a partner, say so from the network, by name and date.
design_moves.why_advantage: Processors report that recent Discover and PULSE releases needed nothing from clients. A light change burden is a real benefit that only processors voice today.

design_moves.title: Operational review for every partner
design_moves.move: Assemble a periodic review from each partner's own record: changes applied, incidents, open cases and attestations due. Offer it to partners without an account manager.
design_moves.why_advantage: Mastercard runs quarterly operational reviews for key accounts and Visa writes client success plans. Small card teams rarely get either. That last point is inference.
